questions.question: In computer system architecture, what is the fundamental defining characteristic of Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) compared to Port-Mapped (Isolated) I/O?
options: All I/O operations bypass the processor bus entirely and communicate directly with system DRAM via an isolated channel.
I/O devices are assigned dedicated address spaces accessible only through specialized CPU instructions like IN and OUT.
The CPU must switch to real mode to execute any read or write transactions destined for peripheral devices.
I/O device registers are mapped into the standard physical memory address space and accessed using standard load and store instructions.
I/O peripherals use optical interconnects rather than electrical traces to synchronize with the system memory controller.

questions.question: In synchronous digital circuit design, what fundamental physical condition causes a bistable element (such as an edge-triggered D flip-flop) to enter a metastable state?
options: The input data transitions exactly when the clock signal is gated off by low-power control logic.
The input data violates the flip-flop's setup or hold time window, leaving internal nodes at an indeterminate voltage between valid logic levels.
The supply voltage drops below the threshold voltage of the pull-up network during a write operation.
The clock tree buffer drives the clock input with a slew rate that is faster than the flip-flop's internal propagation delay.
Ground bounce causes the ground rail to fluctuate above the switching threshold of the master latch's transmission gate.

questions.question: In modern high-performance microprocessors, what is the primary function of Miss Status Holding Registers (MSHRs) in a non-blocking (lockup-free) cache hierarchy?
options: To store evicted dirty cache lines while waiting for a write-back acknowledgment from the main memory bus.
To dynamically record branch outcomes and predict whether future instruction cache misses will be taken or not taken.
To periodically scrub single-bit soft errors in the cache data array using error-correcting codes (ECC).
To enforce cache snooping serialization across multiple cores in a directory-based coherence network.
To track and merge multiple outstanding cache misses, allowing hit-under-miss and miss-under-miss operations without stalling the pipeline.

questions.question: In ASIC physical design and Static Timing Analysis (STA), what is the operational principle of 'useful skew' (clock skew scheduling)?
options: Deliberately adjusting clock arrival times at specific flip-flops to borrow cycle time from non-critical timing paths to fix setup or hold violations on critical paths.
Designing clock tree buffers with identical RC delays so that clock skew is globally reduced to zero across all corners and modes.
Modulating the master phase-locked loop (PLL) clock frequency dynamically based on on-chip temperature sensor feedback.
Aligning the launch and capture clock edges simultaneously to eliminate dynamic power dissipation in the clock distribution network.
Introducing intentional clock jitter to spread electromagnetic interference (EMI) across a wider frequency spectrum.

questions.question: In out-of-order superscalar processor microarchitectures, what is the primary role of speculative memory disambiguation?
options: Translating physical addresses back to virtual addresses during cache line invalidation.
Deciding whether an instruction should be executed in the integer ALU or floating-point unit before instruction decode.
Allowing load instructions to execute speculatively before the addresses of older, uncommitted store instructions are fully resolved.
Preventing multiple threads from accessing the same physical register file in a Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) core.
Dynamically compressing 64-bit memory addresses to 32 bits to reduce TLB tag comparison energy.
